source_architecture_summary: A social-history account traces an industry from scattered local practice through expansion, disruption, technological change, and a smaller transformed afterlife.
feasibility_notes: Blueprint A covers urban rag recovery and paper manufacture; Blueprint B covers telephone answering bureaus. Neither retains natural ice, its geography, dates, or economic figures.

blueprints.blueprint_focus: The rag trade connected household collection to paper mills, expanded through sorting systems, and changed when wood-pulp paper altered material demand.
blueprints.overall_reading_skill_family: Industry chronology, classification, labor, technological disruption, and adaptation
blueprints.rhetorical_or_narrative_arc: Local collection, mill demand, sorting infrastructure, health and price crisis, wood-pulp disruption, specialized survival
blueprints.distinctness_notes: Uses secondary materials and paper manufacture rather than harvested natural resources.

blueprints.blueprint_focus: Telephone answering bureaus grew by pooling operators and lines, faced automation, and survived in specialized services where judgment mattered.
blueprints.overall_reading_skill_family: Service-industry development, infrastructure, labor, automation, and specialization
blueprints.rhetorical_or_narrative_arc: Unanswered-call problem, pooled service growth, operating routines, expansion strain, machine competition, specialized continuity
blueprints.distinctness_notes: Uses information services rather than material collection.
